facts.claim: DARPA's 2026 SBIR success story says Tiqker is moving toward full-scale production, with military/commercial certification and expanded U.S./allied defense deployment as next steps, independently corroborating that precision timing has progressed beyond issuer-only demonstration claims.

The federal SBIR award record identifies a $1.9 million USAF Phase II contract (FA8807-25-C-B001), running through 2026-10-30, to develop a path toward space qualification of Infleqtion's Tiqker optical atomic clock, including ruggedization, manufacturing-yield/cost work and a flight-model design.

risks.risk: Government development funding and a path toward qualification do not establish scaled recurring product revenue, customer concentration, normalized margins or economic quantum-compute advantage.

contradictions.contradiction: Independent government evidence strengthens commercialization/execution for precision timing while the packet's quantum-computing utility and economics remain forward-looking.

unknowns: Current Tiqker unit economics, backlog conversion and recurring commercial revenue remain unverified.
This evidence does not resolve Alpha-owned numeric underwriting or data-confidence construction by itself.
sourcePathsAttempted: DoD/USAF public contract and program records
